item.title: Ally Logistic Property, CapitaLand Investment team up to advance Singapore’s logistics transformation
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Ally Logistic Property (ALP), a logistics infrastructure company, and real asset manager CapitaLand Investment Limited (CLI) have on Friday broke ground on OMEGA 1 Singapore, a S$260 million ($203.51 million) development designed to support Singapore’s next generation of smart logistics infrastructure.
item.content:encoded:
Ally Logistic Property (ALP), a logistics infrastructure company, and real asset manager CapitaLand Investment Limited (CLI) have on Friday broke ground on OMEGA 1 Singapore, a S$260 million ($203.51 million) development designed to support Singapore’s next generation of smart logistics infrastructure.

An asset under CLI’s CapitaLand Southeast Asia Logistics Fund (CSLF), OMEGA 1 Singapore is ALP’s first deployment of its integrated OMEGA logistics infrastructure platform in Singapore, the duo said in a statement.

Developed and proven in Taiwan, OMEGA integrates industrial real estate, shared automation, proprietary software and AI-enabled operational tools within a single platform that helps businesses improve fulfilment speed, operational visibility and supply chain resilience.

OMEGA enables businesses to scale their operations more efficiently without having to bear the significant upfront investment required to develop separate infrastructure and integrate multiple systems.

This supports higher logistics throughput, reduces reliance on labor- intensive processes and allows businesses to expand more flexibly in line with demand.

Targeted for completion in the second half of 2028, OMEGA 1 Singapore will be located at 19 Gul Lane within Singapore’s western industrial and logistics cluster.

Situated near Tuas Port, Tuas Checkpoint and Jurong Port, it will support domestic distribution, regional fulfilment and cross-border logistics flows.

“Logistics infrastructure can no longer be defined by space alone. As supply chains are restructured, labor becomes scarcer, and artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes operations, businesses need infrastructure that connects physical assets, automation, software and intelligence as one system. OMEGA is ALP’s response to that shift,

“Developed in Taiwan and designed for international deployment, it gives companies a more scalable path towards automation, operational resilience and digital transformation. OMEGA 1 Singapore is our first deployment of the platform in Singapore and an important step in ALP’s long-term commitment to the country’s logistics transformation,” said Charlie Chang, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of ALP.

Patricia Goh, Chief Executive Officer, Southeast Asia and Global Head, Logistics & Self-Storage, CapitaLand Investment, said demand from institutional investors and occupiers for technology-enabled logistics infrastructure continues to grow across Asia Pacific.

This is driven by structural trends such as labor shortages arising from an ageing population, e-commerce growth, and the AI-driven transformation of business processes and supply chains, she noted.

“As we continue to expand our logistics footprint across key Asia Pacific markets, we remain focused on developing future-ready assets through selective development and asset enhancement opportunities,

“These investments will strengthen CLI’s differentiated logistics operating capabilities and support the growth of our listed and private funds management platform,” she added.

As fulfilment volumes continue to grow, Singapore’s logistics sector faces persistent land and labor constraints, alongside the increasing complexity of integrating physical infrastructure, automation, software and systems.

OMEGA 1 Singapore is designed to address these challenges through shared and standardized infrastructure that can help businesses adopt advanced logistics capabilities more efficiently and scale their operations over time.

More broadly, OMEGA 1 Singapore aims to introduce a scalable logistics infrastructure model that supports Singapore’s position as a critical regional and global trade hub, while helping businesses automate, expand and respond more effectively to evolving supply-chain needs.

“Optimizing land use and adopting technology at scale will be critical to Singapore’s next phase of logistics growth,

“OMEGA 1 Singapore demonstrates how innovative infrastructure partnerships can support a more competitive and future-ready logistics ecosystem, reinforcing Singapore’s role as a leading global trade and logistics hub,” said Jacqueline Poh, Chief Executive Officer, JTC Corporation.

Ho Weng Si, Executive Vice President, Economic Development Board (EDB), said OMEGA 1 Singapore delivers integrated, automation-ready infrastructure to support companies’ regional distribution operations.

“This investment highlights continued confidence in Singapore’s logistics ecosystem and reinforces our ongoing efforts to scale automation and build digital capabilities across the sector, creating good job opportunities for locals,” she added.

OMEGA reflects ALP’s vision to reshape how logistics infrastructure is designed, delivered and operated.

OMEGA 1 Singapore marks an important step in ALP’s broader ambition to expand the OMEGA platform across major regional and international markets.

In Southeast Asia, ALP already has OMEGA facilities operating or under development in Malaysia and Thailand.

Under CSLF, OMEGA 1 Bang Na, a built-to-suit smart logistics campus, is being developed in the Greater Bangkok Metropolitan Area.

It will be Thailand’s largest standalone logistics campus, with phase 1 of the facility expected to be completed by the end of September 2026.

Through OMEGA, ALP is moving beyond the conventional logistics property model to establish a new generation of integrated infrastructure for the industry.

The OMEGA platform’s core infrastructure can be replicated across markets and adapted to local regulatory, sustainability and operational requirements.

This allows ALP to apply a consistent model while responding to the needs of different industries and supply chains, said the statement.

Singapore unveils SG Semiconductor to strengthen its role in the global semiconductor ecosystem

item.title: Singapore unveils SG Semiconductor to strengthen its role in the global semiconductor ecosystem
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Singapore has on Friday announced SG Semiconductor, a national identity for Singapore’s semiconductor sector.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore has on Friday announced SG Semiconductor, a national identity for Singapore’s semiconductor sector.

Jointly developed by A*STAR and the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB), SG Semiconductor will raise the global visibility of Singapore’s sector-wide strengths and make it easier for companies and talent to understand what the country offers and engage its ecosystem, EDB said in a statement.

The branding effort will focus on public sector research and development (R&D) as its first course of action.

SG Semiconductor brings together Singapore’s capabilities across R&D, advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, industry partnerships and talent.

Its work spans seven technology areas: advanced packaging, silicon photonics, power electronics, radio frequency gallium nitride, piezoelectric micro-electro-mechanical systems (piezoMEMS), flat optics and integrated circuit design.

Across these areas, Singapore is developing capabilities to address growing needs in artificial intelligence and advanced computing, high-speed and energy-efficient data communications, electrification, sensing and intelligent systems.

By connecting research expertise with industry-grade infrastructure and manufacturing capabilities of industry partners, Singapore can develop, validate and scale new semiconductor technologies for global markets.

It is noted that Singapore has built a substantial semiconductor industry over nearly six decades, spanning chip design, wafer fabrication, assembly and testing, equipment and materials development and manufacturing, and R&D.

It now accounts for one in ten global chip output and one-fifth of global semiconductor manufacturing equipment production.

As applications become more sophisticated and place greater demands on semiconductor performance, Singapore is building on this foundation through closer research-industry collaboration and talent development, supported by the latest S$800 million ($626 million) investment from 2026 to 2030 through the RIE Flagship in Semiconductors.

“Singapore’s strength in semiconductor innovation has been built through decades of sustained investment and close partnership across public research, universities and industry,

“SG Semiconductor brings this collective endeavor under a national identity. It signals our commitment to build frontier capabilities, translate them into industry outcomes and anchor high-value R&D and manufacturing in Singapore for the long term,” said Beh Kian Teik, Chief Executive, A*STAR.

Jermaine Loy, Managing Director of EDB, said as semiconductor technologies become more complex, companies are increasingly seeking trusted locations where innovation, manufacturing and talent come together.

“SG Semiconductor provides a gateway to Singapore’s ecosystem, enabling companies to develop, scale and commercialise next-generation technologies from Singapore,” he added.

Demonstrating SG Semiconductor in action, Innovate Together 2026 also saw the announcement of new and expanded partnerships spanning several key semiconductor technology areas.

These collaborations connect research expertise with industry-grade platforms and manufacturing capabilities to develop, validate and scale emerging technologies.

In advanced packaging, Applied Materials and A*STAR will embark on Phase 4 of their longstanding collaboration, significantly expanding the joint laboratory’s infrastructure, equipment and headcount to develop technologies for AI and advanced computing.

A*STAR and KLA will establish a new process control collaboration framework to explore ways to improve manufacturing reliability and yield, while A*STAR and STATS ChipPAC will collaborate in co-packaged optics to create a pathway towards high-volume production.

Together, these collaborations strengthen Singapore’s position as a hub for advanced packaging innovation and help accelerate the translation of next-generation semiconductor technologies into manufacturing.

In silicon photonics, A*STAR and GlobalFoundries will deepen their R&D collaboration to develop next-generation technologies on 300 mm wafers in Singapore, supporting higher-volume manufacturing for high-performance computing and data communications.

This will help bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and commercial-scale production, supporting growing global demand for high-speed, energy-efficient connectivity solutions.

In MEMS sensing, Tacta Systems and A*STAR will develop intelligent sensing technologies for robotics, tapping A*STAR’s Lab-in-Fab platform, which brings together research and manufacturing capabilities for industry-relevant development, prototyping and validation.

Tacta Systems has also opened its Singapore operations, strengthening its technology development activities here.

The wider ecosystem represented by SG Semiconductor includes a new research collaboration between National Center for Advanced Integrated Photonics (NCAIP), a national center hosted at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and Battery Age Minerals.

The partners will explore germanium-based devices for data communications by combining NTU’s research expertise with Battery Age Minerals’ access to raw germanium, creating a potential pathway from upstream resources to higher-value semiconductor applications.

The collaboration highlights how Singapore’s ecosystem brings together partners across the global value chain to explore new opportunities and create future sources of semiconductor innovation.

“These partnerships demonstrate Singapore’s ability to bring together world-class research, industry-grade platforms and advanced manufacturing capabilities to move emerging technologies from concept to commercialization,

“SG Semiconductor will strengthen this advantage by giving companies a clearer path to translate innovation into globally competitive products and scale them for international markets,“ said Professor Yeo Yee Chia, Deputy Chief Executive (Innovation & Enterprise), A*STAR and Executive Vice President of the RIE2030 Flagship in Semiconductors.

StarHub in talks to buy M1 from Keppel in Singapore telecom consolidation

item.title: StarHub in talks to buy M1 from Keppel in Singapore telecom consolidation
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Singapore-based telecommunications StarHub is in discussions with conglomerate Keppel over a possible transaction involving M1, Singapore's third-largest telecommunications operator.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore-based telecommunications StarHub is in discussions with conglomerate Keppel over a possible transaction involving M1, Singapore’s third-largest telecommunications operator.

StarHub made the confirmation in a filing with the Singapore Exchange (SGX), dated September 23. The talks are preliminary, with no certainty of an agreement, StarHub said.

M1 is Singapore’s third-largest mobile operator and is controlled by Keppel, a Singapore conglomerate that took the telco private in 2019. StarHub is the country’s second-largest operator, behind Singtel.

A combination of StarHub and M1 would be the first major consolidation among Singapore’s mobile carriers.

The talks follow the collapse earlier in 2026 of a proposed sale of M1’s telecom business to Simba for about S$1.43 ($1.12 billion). That deal stalled after the Singapore’s Infocomm Media Development Authority suspended its review amid an investigation into Simba.

A StarHub–M1 tie-up would bring together two companies linked to Temasek, Singapore’s state investment firm and a controlling shareholder of both StarHub and Keppel.

Singapore suspends review of proposed $1.1B M1-Simba telco consolidation

item.title: Asian developers lean on AI agents, still 86% needs human review: Agoda
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Software developers across Southeast Asia and India are handing more work to autonomous AI "agents," yet 86 percent still have to review or validate the AI's output most of the time
item.content:encoded:
Software developers across Southeast Asia and India are handing more work to autonomous AI “agents,” yet 86 percent still have to review or validate the AI’s output most of the time

Singapore-based digital travel platform Agoda, part of Booking Holdings, released the figure in its “Agoda AI Developer Report 2026.” The report, released on Friday, showed that 79 percent of AI tasks require human approval before code reaches production.

The Agoda AI Developer Report 2026, based on responses from more than 800 developers and engineering leaders across seven markets, found that 53 percent now use AI agents in selected production workflows or broadly across their organisations. This is a shift from earlier assistant-style use.

Adoption was highest in Thailand at 64 percent, followed by Vietnam at 59 percent, and Singapore at 58 percent. Only 38 percent considered their codebase ready for full autonomy, meaning some teams are deploying agents into code they do not yet regard as ready.

Productivity gains have risen sharply. The share of developers saving at least seven hours a week tripled to 55 percent from 18 percent in 2025, the report said. The figure varied, such as Thailand at 70 percent, Vietnam at 63 percent and the Philippines at 57 percent. About 62 percent said AI-generated code was usable often or almost always without major changes.

Cost has become a leading obstacle to wider use, cited by 28 percent as the top barrier, narrowly ahead of integration complexity at 24 percent and weak governance at 19 percent. The report said AI costs extend beyond model usage to the work of designing, integrating and validating agents, and that four in five developers operate under some limit such as token quotas or budget caps.

The demand for oversight tightens closer to production, with the human sign-off requirement rising to 84 percent in both Vietnam and Thailand. Even so, 71 percent expect AI agents to handle most development work within three years.

Idan Zalzberg, Agoda’s chief technology officer, said AI was moving from speeding up individual tasks to reshaping software development more broadly, but that the real cost lay in making AI trustworthy in production.

The survey was conducted online between June and August 2026 with Macramé Consulting, covering India, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

Agoda opens new APAC tech hub in Bangkok

item.title: Vietnam’s Stavian starts U.S.-backed feasibility study for Ho Chi Minh City AI data-center project
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Stavian Group, a Vietnamese infrastructure developer, with backing from a U.S. government agency, has begun a feasibility study for a large AI and cloud data-center campus planned in Ho Chi Minh City.
item.content:encoded:
Stavian Group, a Vietnamese infrastructure developer, with backing from a U.S. government agency, has begun a feasibility study for a large AI and cloud data-center campus planned in Ho Chi Minh City.

In a statement on Friday, Stavian said its group member Stavian Hightech Infrastructure has appointed Cushman & Wakefield to lead the study for the campus. The project, called Stavian Digital Park, is funded by a grant from the U.S. Trade and Development Agency (USTDA).

Telecommunications specialist APTelecom will work under Cushman & Wakefield on connectivity and digital-infrastructure planning, market development, commercialization strategy, and financial modelling.

The study comprises 15 workstreams covering market demand, site suitability, power, connectivity, cooling, financial viability, sustainability, regulation, and implementation. It will produce a master plan, financial model, and procurement framework.

As planned, the campus would span 300 hectares as a carrier-neutral development, with 300 MW of power in a first phase by 2030 and access to international subsea connectivity of up to 200 Tb per second, according to Stavian.

It can serve global cloud providers, enterprises, government systems, content-delivery networks, and AI workloads, with on-site solar and other renewable energy planned to lower its carbon footprint.

USTDA said the study would help attract financing and position U.S. companies to supply technology. The campus would use “trusted” technology and require customers to use secure equipment, the USTDA added.

The agency said the project fit its broader work on trusted, resilient digital infrastructure in the Indo-Pacific, including subsea cables linking Southeast Asian markets and the United States. The campus can attract hyperscale cloud and AI operators, including U.S. firms, as first customers.

Thomas R. Hardy, USTDA’s deputy director, said the partnership laid the groundwork for a project on trusted technology and would help meet Vietnam’s digital-infrastructure needs while creating openings for American firms.

Vietnam’s data center operator CMC, Viettel petition ministry over power pricing after cutoff threat

item.title: AnyMind adds Alibaba Qwen models to AnyLive’s AI commerce stack
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: AnyMind Group is integrating Alibaba's Qwen models into AnyLive to improve real-time intent analysis and Asian-language responses for AI-led live commerce.
item.content:encoded:
AnyMind Group is adding Alibaba’s Qwen models to the multi-model AI architecture behind AnyLive, its live-commerce platform, as the company looks to improve real-time intent analysis and responses across Asian languages.

The companies announced the strategic agreement on September 24. Qwen will operate as one model within AnyLive rather than replacing the platform’s wider model stack, according to AnyMind’s announcement.

TNGlobal has recently covered AnyLive’s updated AI avatars and cross-stream analytics and AnyMind’s expansion of live-commerce operations in Indonesia.

Qwen joins a multi-model stack

AnyMind said Qwen will be used to strengthen how its AI avatars interpret ambiguous customer questions and generate contextually relevant answers during live-commerce sessions.

The integration is aimed particularly at Asian-language interactions, where language choice, honorifics, code-switching and local phrasing can affect whether an automated host correctly understands what a viewer is asking.

AnyLive is designed to let brands run AI-fronted live streams alongside human-hosted sessions. AnyMind has positioned the AI layer primarily as a way to extend selling hours and handle routine product explanation outside peak periods, while human presenters remain important for higher-engagement sessions.

Language quality becomes an operating constraint

In a live-commerce environment, a model has to respond while the shopper is still watching. That makes both intent recognition and response latency important. An answer that is technically correct but arrives too late, uses the wrong level of formality or misunderstands a mixed-language question can still produce a poor interaction.

AnyMind said the Qwen integration is intended to improve fluency and local context across the Asian markets where it operates. The company has not disclosed comparative benchmark results showing how Qwen performs against the other models in AnyLive’s stack, or how much the integration changes conversion rates.

Always-on commerce remains the commercial pitch

One of AnyLive’s main use cases is extending commerce coverage into hours when a brand would not normally keep a human host on camera. AnyMind said the integration can help leaner teams operate across several markets while maintaining round-the-clock live-commerce availability.

That does not remove the need for human oversight. In a recent TNGlobal Q&A, AnyMind Managing Director of Global E-Commerce Kubo Akinori said AI avatars are most useful for scalable product expertise and off-peak coverage, while human hosts remain important for entertainment, storytelling and high-impact campaign moments.

That division of labor also puts more pressure on measurement. Brands need to distinguish incremental sales or customer interactions generated during AI-covered hours from purchases that would have happened through another channel anyway.

Alibaba extends Qwen into commerce workflows

For Alibaba Cloud, the agreement puts Qwen into another production commerce workflow outside Alibaba’s own consumer platforms. The model family has been expanding across enterprise, agentic and multimodal use cases as Alibaba builds a broader full-stack AI strategy.

For AnyMind, the partnership adds another model provider to an architecture the company describes as multi-model. That approach gives the platform room to use different models for different tasks rather than binding every live-commerce function to one model family.

The companies did not disclose financial terms for the agreement, customer commitments tied to the integration or a specific rollout schedule by market.

AnyMind updates AnyLive with more lifelike AI avatars and cross-stream analytics

item.title: Akamai signs $11.6 billion cloud agreement with Anthropic
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Akamai has signed a seven-year cloud services agreement with Anthropic carrying $11.6 billion in contractual commitments, with room to expand by $9 billion.
item.content:encoded:
Akamai Technologies has signed a seven-year cloud services agreement with Anthropic carrying $11.6 billion in contractual commitments, as the Claude developer expands the computing infrastructure behind its artificial-intelligence products.

Under the agreement announced on September 24, Anthropic will use Akamai Cloud’s distributed infrastructure and software to support growing central processing unit workloads. The companies may expand the relationship by up to an additional $9 billion over the same term, which Akamai describes as a total potential commitment of approximately $20 billion.

The announcement does not disclose capacity, service pricing, a deployment timetable or how the workloads will be distributed geographically. It refers specifically to CPU workloads rather than a dedicated graphics processing unit training buildout.

Agreement links cloud spending to an equity warrant

Akamai has issued Anthropic a warrant to buy non-voting convertible Series B preferred stock representing 7.7 million Akamai common shares on an as-converted basis. If fully vested and exercised, the warrant could give Anthropic the equivalent of approximately 5 percent of Akamai’s outstanding common stock.

The exercise price is $111.33 per common-equivalent share. A portion representing approximately 2 percent of Akamai’s outstanding common stock is expected to vest in connection with the initial $11.6 billion commitment.

The remaining approximately 3 percent is conditional on expansion of the commercial relationship. Each additional $3 billion purchase of cloud services on mutually agreed terms would cause another approximately 1 percent portion to vest. The potential $9 billion expansion is therefore neither part of the current committed amount nor guaranteed.

Akamai shares rose 22 percent in extended trading after the announcement, according to Reuters coverage carried by CNA. The warrant gives Anthropic a potential equity interest in the infrastructure provider, but it should not be treated as a current 5 percent holding.

Akamai plans $5.5 billion in related capital spending

Akamai estimates total capital expenditure related to the initial commitment at approximately $5.5 billion. It expects to increase 2026 capital spending by approximately $1.7 billion to secure and pre-purchase critical supply-chain components, including memory.

The company said the agreement would not affect its 2026 revenue guidance. The $11.6 billion figure is a contractual commitment covering seven years, not revenue to be recognized immediately, and Akamai did not disclose the expected annual revenue schedule or contract margins.

The deal adds to more than $2.8 billion in multi-year Cloud Infrastructure Services commitments that Akamai said it had previously announced across its customer base this year. In May, Akamai disclosed that an unnamed frontier-model provider had made a $1.8 billion, seven-year commitment for the same business. The September announcement calls the Anthropic relationship significantly expanded but does not specify how the earlier commitment is treated within the new figure.

Deal deepens Akamai’s AI infrastructure push

Akamai is positioning its network of core and edge facilities as an alternative source of compute for AI companies seeking capacity beyond the largest cloud platforms. Its cloud network spans thousands of points of presence and uses a mix of hardware intended to run and deliver applications closer to users.

Chief Executive Tom Leighton said the agreement reflected Anthropic’s choice of Akamai for “building and operating AI infrastructure at scale.” That statement remains a company assessment; the release provides no performance benchmarks, committed service levels or workload volumes for the Anthropic deployment.

The size of the contract illustrates how AI developers are locking in long-term infrastructure as model usage grows, while providers invest ahead of the associated revenue. For Akamai, execution will depend on obtaining components, bringing capacity online and meeting Anthropic’s requirements without materially weakening returns.

For Anthropic, the agreement broadens its infrastructure supplier base. The companies did not disclose whether the new Akamai capacity will replace other providers or operate alongside them, and no Asia-Pacific capacity allocation was announced.

Akamai Unveils Akamai Connected Cloud and New Cloud Computing Services

item.title: Thailand approves semiconductor strategy targeting $80B investment
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.category: National Semiconductor and Advanced Electronics Policy Board
item.description: Thailand has approved its first national semiconductor strategy, targeting about $80 billion in cumulative investment and more than 230,000 jobs by 2050.
item.content:encoded:
Thailand has approved its first national semiconductor and advanced electronics strategy, setting a target of about $80 billion in cumulative investment and more than 230,000 new jobs by 2050 as it seeks to build a more complete domestic chip supply chain.

The strategy was approved by the National Semiconductor and Advanced Electronics Policy Board, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas, according to the Thailand Board of Investment (BOI). Reuters separately reported the targets following the September 24 announcement.

Roadmap moves upstream

The three-phase roadmap starts with Thailand’s established strengths in semiconductor assembly and testing. By 2030, the government plans to expand advanced packaging and prepare for front-end wafer production. By 2040, it aims to attract more investment in chip design, wafer fabrication and other upstream manufacturing. The 2050 goal is a complete domestic supply chain.

The strategy prioritizes three technology platforms. Photonics is aimed at artificial intelligence infrastructure, data centers and high-speed communications. Power semiconductors are tied to electric vehicles, energy storage and power grids, while sensors build on Thailand’s existing micro-electro-mechanical systems capabilities.

The BOI said implementation will combine tax incentives, grants and low-interest financing with workforce development, research and chip-design infrastructure, industrial sites, reliable utilities and regulatory reforms.

Workforce plan targets 86,600 people by 2030

A workforce program approved alongside the strategy aims to develop 86,600 people by 2030, including 84,900 highly skilled personnel and about 1,700 advanced researchers. The program will involve universities, research institutes and industry partners through specialized curricula, industry placements and overseas training.

Thailand has already been drawing semiconductor and advanced electronics projects. The BOI said it received investment-promotion applications for 879 projects worth about 909 billion baht, or $27.2 billion, from 2023 through the first half of 2026. Those figures represent applications rather than capital already deployed.

The new approval formalizes a direction that Thailand had been developing earlier this year. TNGlobal reported in January that the semiconductor board was reviewing a draft strategy with phased targets through 2050. The final plan retains the broad investment and workforce ambitions while setting out the implementation framework.

Infineon factory adds near-term capacity

The announcement also comes ahead of Infineon Technologies’ planned October 1 opening of its first factory in Thailand, in Samut Prakan. According to the BOI, the facility will produce and package advanced power modules for electric vehicles, energy storage, clean energy and advanced electronics. Infineon also plans an R&D center and joint curricula with Thai educational institutions.

Thailand’s electronics investment pipeline has expanded beyond semiconductors. In August, TNGlobal reported that the country had attracted more than $30.5 billion in electronics investment since 2023, including projects involving printed circuit boards, components and semiconductor-related products.

Featured image: Laura Ockel on Unsplash

Thailand maps long-term semiconductor strategy, pushes toward full value chain

item.title: CBAK signs deal for 12 GWh sodium-ion battery project in Nanjing
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: CBAK Energy has signed an investment agreement for a planned 12 GWh battery project in Nanjing that can produce sodium-ion or lithium-ion cells.
item.content:encoded:
China-based CBAK Energy Technology has signed an investment agreement with the Nanjing Gaochun Economic Development Zone for a planned 12 gigawatt-hour annual battery-cell project focused on large cylindrical sodium-ion and lithium-ion batteries.

The Nasdaq-listed company said the project would cover cell manufacturing as well as module and battery-pack integration in Nanjing, Jiangsu Province. Development is planned in phases and remains subject to financing, customer demand and project readiness.

Project could add 12 GWh of capacity

CBAK plans to advance the 12 GWh project in the second half of 2027, subject to securing financing. The proposed production lines would be designed to make either sodium-ion or lithium-ion cells, allowing the company to select the chemistry according to market conditions and customer demand.

The company estimated that the project could generate RMB4.8 billion to RMB5.0 billion, about $712 million to $741 million, in annual revenue if it operates at full capacity and sells all output. CBAK explicitly described those figures as estimates based on current lithium-ion cell market prices rather than contracted sales or financial guidance.

Customer testing of CBAK’s sodium-ion samples is underway for residential and portable energy storage and electric-mobility applications, according to the company. Other evaluations cover specialty vehicles, start-stop systems and backup power.

Existing Nanjing plant also set to expand

Separately, CBAK plans to add another 6 GWh of annual cell capacity at its existing Nanjing facility by the end of 2026. The plant currently has 4.5 GWh of annual Model 32140 cell capacity, and the planned addition would raise the total to 10.5 GWh.

The company is considering two production lines for its Model 60150 large cylindrical cells, although it may install one Model 32140 line and one Model 60150 line depending on demand. At full capacity with all incremental output sold, CBAK estimates the 6 GWh expansion could generate RMB2.4 billion to RMB2.7 billion, or about $356 million to $400 million, in annual revenue.

CBAK has been expanding the Nanjing site for several years. Earlier TNGlobal coverage detailed equipment procurement for a 3 GWh Phase II expansion involving large cylindrical lithium-ion cells.

Sodium-ion manufacturing moves toward larger scale

Sodium-ion batteries are drawing investment as manufacturers look beyond conventional lithium-ion chemistries for energy storage and mobility. The technology uses more abundant sodium-based materials, although commercial performance and economics vary by chemistry and application.

Chinese battery companies have been moving sodium-ion products toward commercial-scale deployments. In June, CATL unveiled a sodium-ion energy storage system and said global deliveries were planned from June 2027. CBAK’s proposed Nanjing project adds another potential source of large-scale capacity, although its timing remains dependent on financing and customer qualification.

The flexibility to manufacture either sodium-ion or lithium-ion cells also limits how much of the proposed 12 GWh should be treated as committed sodium-ion capacity. CBAK said the final production mix will depend on market conditions, while the development itself will proceed in phases.

CBAK Energy Announces Expansion in Nanjing: Equipment Procurement Completed and Trial Production Set for May 2025, Adding 3GWh of Capacity

item.title: Singapore fintech iPiD raises $16M Series A led by Foundation Capital
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Singapore-headquartered payment intelligence firm iPiD has raised $16 million in a Series A led by Foundation Capital, with Citi and HSBC participating.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore-headquartered payment intelligence company iPiD has raised $16 million in a Series A round led by Foundation Capital, with participation from Citi and HSBC, as it expands its payee-verification network and develops new capabilities for faster payment rails and digital assets.

The company announced the funding on September 24. Existing investors QED Investors, Monk’s Hill Ventures and Quona Capital also joined the round. Axios separately reported the financing and said iPiD is expanding account-verification coverage as instant payments reduce the time available to catch mistakes and fraud before funds move.

Funding backs payment intelligence expansion

iPiD said the new capital will support expansion of its global payment intelligence network, growth in the United States and Europe, and development of products for U.S. payment rails, stablecoins and other digital assets.

The company focuses on payee verification, helping banks, payment providers and businesses confirm whether a recipient account is valid and whether account details match the intended beneficiary before a transfer is executed. It describes the approach as “Know Your Payee,” complementing know-your-customer checks that focus on the sender.

iPiD said its network now reaches financial institutions in more than 50 countries. Axios reported that the company says it can reach more than 6,500 financial institutions and about 4 billion bank accounts through direct connections and distribution partners. Those coverage figures are company-supplied.

The business is positioning its verification layer around a payments environment in which real-time transfers are becoming more common and increasingly difficult to reverse. Faster settlement can improve user experience, but it also leaves banks and senders with less time to detect a wrong account number, mismatched beneficiary or fraudulent destination.

Citi and HSBC join as strategic investors

Citi and HSBC participated as strategic investors in the round. Both institutions also have commercial relationships with iPiD.

iPiD said Citi uses its technology as part of Citi Verify, while HSBC uses the company to extend beneficiary-validation capabilities beyond local verification schemes. The company’s broader customer and partner list includes Visa, Nium, Experian, Tazapay and other payment and financial-services providers.

Foundation Capital partner Zach Noorani said in the company’s announcement that iPiD has built a global verification layer outside the traditional bank-consortium model. Citi and HSBC executives also highlighted the role of beneficiary verification in reducing payment uncertainty and improving fraud controls.

The strategic participation of major banks gives the funding round a commercial dimension beyond capital. iPiD’s product depends on access to fragmented local banking and payment systems, making distribution relationships and institutional integrations important to expanding coverage.

Series A follows earlier Singapore funding rounds

iPiD was founded in 2021 by payments executives with experience at SWIFT and other financial-technology companies. The company is headquartered in Singapore and also operates across markets including London, New York, Dubai, Amsterdam, Brussels, Kuala Lumpur and Mumbai.

The Series A follows two earlier rounds covered by TNGlobal. In 2022, iPiD raised $3.3 million in seed funding from investors including Rapyd Ventures, Jungle Ventures, 1982 Ventures and others. In 2024, the company closed a $5.3 million pre-Series A led by Monk’s Hill Ventures, with QED Investors and Quona Capital participating.

The new financing takes iPiD into a larger institutional expansion phase. The company is also looking beyond conventional bank-account verification toward stablecoin wallets and other digital-payment destinations, according to its announcement and Axios.

iPiD did not disclose its valuation in the funding announcement. It also did not provide a timetable for the planned U.S. and digital-asset product expansions. As with its coverage and performance figures, those future deployment plans should be treated as company targets until additional products or customer rollouts are announced.
